IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated GPU memory growth and allocator fragmentation observed in inference-pool-3 (us-west-2). Symptoms: steady increase in allocated arena extents causing repeated continuous-batching blowups and latency cliffs. Paging @Sam (oncall) and SRE team.
Sam: oncall here, looking now. any customer-facing errors yet?
Priya: seeing a bunch of 503s and gRPC timeouts for long-sequence generation jobs. tail latencies spiking to >30s for some requests. Not full pod OOMs yet but memory usage keeps creeping.
Jordan: captured allocator stats from one worker, past 30m:
```
GPU0: total_alloc=28.3G, cached=22.1G, active_arenas=13, fragmentation_pct=46, kv_cache_size=9.2G, batch_size_median=64
worker: continuous-batching queue length jumped 3x at 09:12 UTC
```
Priya: looks like the KV/cache growth correlates with very long prefix requests (~>4k tokens) that keep KV shards pinned and prevent effective eviction. eviction policy is currently conservative.
Sam: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cap per-request max_batch_tokens to 512 for the pool, 2) temporarily enable aggressive KV eviction (ttl->30s), 3) roll workers with modified TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF to encourage smaller arena splits. I'll stage the config change now.
Sam: applying feature flag to pool 'inference-pool-3' (hotfix). curl command:
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.internal.redwood/api/v1/pools/inference-pool-3/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"max_batch_tokens":512,"kv_eviction_policy":"aggressive","kv_eviction_ttl_s":30}'
```
DeployBot: Deploy of config change started for inference-pool-3 by Sam at 09:22 UTC. Instances: 12 -> rolling restart.
Alice: +1 - will watch traces and roll out canary across 3 instances first.
Marco: after canary roll, memory curve drops on those instances but others still drifting upward. overall error rate down from 7.8% -> 3.2% in the last 6m. customer impact narrowed to ~2% of requests: heavy long-sequence workloads.
Jordan: added a short patch to runtime to export allocator histograms on /metrics for faster triage (PR: #4823). snippet:
```go
// expose arena histograms
metrics.Gauge("gpu.arena_extents").Set(arena.Extents())
```
Priya: noticed GC-like churn in arenas — I think the PyTorch caching allocator is creating many small splits. Suggest we set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF on workers: `max_split_size_mb:32` and `garbage_collection_threshold:0` and then roll. That should reduce fragmentation.
Sam: agreed. I'll trigger a worker relaunch with env override for the next wave. Rolling now for remaining 9 instances.
Sam: also bumped batch backpressure threshold to reduce continuous-batching accumulation: set `continuous_batch_max_batches=8` on the pool.
Marco: after the full roll (09:36 UTC) memory growth flattened and fragmentation metric decreased to ~18%. tail latency improved to 95th=1.2s from 95th=3.8s. :white_check_mark:
Priya: running verification against known offender prompt set (long-seq smoke): 1000 runs: error rate 0.8%, median latency 1.1s. still seeing 5 slow outliers — correlating with an older model variant pinned to customers.
Sam: immediate customer impact: broad degradation mitigated; a small cohort (enterprise customers pinned to model-v1.9) still saw degraded performance. I notified Support to open targeted CS tickets and offered to migrate them to model-v2 temporarily.
Jordan: logging note: saved heap/allocator trace for one affected worker: `/var/log/inference/allocator-dump-2837771234.log` (uploaded to incident artifacts).
Alice: suggested longer-term actions: 1) update default eviction policy for pools with long-seq traffic, 2) add an automated canary that simulates long prefix loads every 4h, 3) schedule allocator compaction work.
Priya: starting a focused follow-up: reproduce fragmentation locally using long-seq harness, test different `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` values, and run microbench for continuous-batching behavior. assigning to Marco + Priya.
Sam: will keep paging rotation informed. Handoff to next oncall (Jordan) at 11:00 UTC. Creating incident ticket and initial severity: Sev2 (customer impact limited to specific customers but risk of broader regression).
Sam: postmortem owner: Priya, secondary: Marco. I'll add timelines and mitigation steps.
Marco: throwing in a tiny hotfix that forces arena compaction every N cycles as a safe guard. small diff:
```diff
diff --git a/runtime/allocator/arena.cc b/runtime/allocator/arena.cc
@@ -112,6 +112,10 @@ void Arena::maybe_compact() {
-  if (free_ratio < 0.2) return;
+  // force periodic compaction to avoid runaway fragmentation under long-seq
+  if (cycle_count % 100 == 0 || free_ratio < 0.2) {
+    compact_locked();
+  }
```

Marco: will open PR for the compaction heuristic (PR: #4824) and mark it for fasttrack review.
DeployBot: PR #4824 merged and rolled to stages at 10:55 UTC (canary OK).
Sam: final status @ 10:58 UTC: mitigation successful, pool stable, error rates back to baseline except for the pinned customer cohort; follow-ups and postmortem assigned. Handoff complete.
Priya: adding runbook note: if fragmentation detected (fragmentation_pct > 35 and continuous-batch queue > 2x baseline) -> cap max_batch_tokens, enable aggressive eviction, roll TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF, and schedule immediate compaction run.
Sam: thanks all. tagging @incident-management for blameless postmortem.
